newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's KCRC awards Western rail studies contracts.
newsitem.headline: HK's KCRC awards Western rail studies contracts.

text.p: The Kowloon-Canton Railway Corp (KCRC) said on Tuesday it had awarded two technical study contracts worth HK$7.2 million for phase two of the Western Corridor Railway project.

The Association of American Railroads Transportation Technology Center and private researcher Battelle won the two contracts, the first of 14 studies on the second phase of the project, the government-owned KCRC said in a statement.
Of the remaining 12 studies, three were under pre-qualification, three were about to be tendered and six had been issued for tender, it said.
The proposed rail line would link the northwestern New Territories and central Kowloon, with construction anticipated to begin in mid-1998.
Last December, the government said it would build the project's domestic passenger line first, leaving the cross-border and freight lines to a later date.
Transport secretary Gordon Siu has said the project would require HK$24 billion in direct government support, although the figures would be refined as the KCRC proceeded with its studies.
